legend: Consider some set of distinct characters A%%ZSMJ0%% and some string S%%ZSMJ1%%, consisting of exactly n%%ZSMJ2%% characters, where each character is present in A%%ZSMJ3%%.
You are given an array of m%%ZSMJ4%% integers b%%ZSMJ5%% (b1<b2<⋯<bm%%ZSMJ6%%).
You are allowed to perform the following move on the string S%%ZSMJ7%%:
Choose some valid i%%ZSMJ8%% and set k=bi%%ZSMJ9%%;
Take the first k%%ZSMJ10%% characters of S=Prk%%ZSMJ11%%;
Take the last k%%ZSMJ12%% characters of S=Suk%%ZSMJ13%%;
Substitute the first k%%ZSMJ14%% characters of S%%ZSMJ15%% with the reversed Suk%%ZSMJ16%%;
Substitute the last k%%ZSMJ17%% characters of S%%ZSMJ18%% with the reversed Prk%%ZSMJ19%%.

For example, let's take a look at S=%%ZSMJ20%% "abcdefghi" and k=2%%ZSMJ21%%. Pr2=%%ZSMJ22%% "ab", Su2=%%ZSMJ23%% "hi". Reversed Pr2=%%ZSMJ24%% "ba", Su2=%%ZSMJ25%% "ih". Thus, the resulting S%%ZSMJ26%% is "ihcdefgba".
The move can be performed arbitrary number of times (possibly zero). Any i%%ZSMJ27%% can be selected multiple times over these moves.

Let's call some strings S%%ZSMJ28%% and T%%ZSMJ29%% equal if and only if there exists such a sequence of moves to transmute string S%%ZSMJ30%% to string T%%ZSMJ31%%. For the above example strings "abcdefghi" and "ihcdefgba" are equal. Also note that this implies S=S%%ZSMJ32%%.
The task is simple. Count the number of distinct strings.
The answer can be huge enough, so calculate it modulo 998244353%%ZSMJ33%%.
input: The first line contains three integers n%%ZSMJ34%%, m%%ZSMJ35%% and |A|%%ZSMJ36%% (2≤n≤109%%ZSMJ37%%, 1≤m≤min(n2,2⋅105)%%ZSMJ38%%, 1≤|A|≤109%%ZSMJ39%%) — the length of the strings, the size of the array b%%ZSMJ40%% and the size of the set A%%ZSMJ41%%, respectively.
The second line contains m%%ZSMJ42%% integers b1,b2,…,bm%%ZSMJ43%% (1≤bi≤n2%%ZSMJ44%%, b1<b2<⋯<bm%%ZSMJ45%%).
output: Print a single integer — the number of distinct strings of length n%%ZSMJ46%% with characters from set A%%ZSMJ47%% modulo 998244353%%ZSMJ48%%.
note: Here are all the distinct strings for the first example. The chosen letters 'a' and 'b' are there just to show that the characters in A%%ZSMJ49%% are different.
